name: Supported 90/90 psoas relaxation
notes: Lie on your back with calves resting on a chair, hips and knees bent about 90°. Breathe slowly into the lower ribs and abdomen; allow your lower back and hips to relax. Do not force your back flat.
origin: New addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Lie on your back beside a sturdy chair.
Rest both calves on the seat with hips and knees near right angles.
Relax your shoulders and breathe slowly without forcing your spine flat.

name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch with posterior pelvic tilt
notes: Kneel on a padded surface with one foot forward. Gently tuck your tailbone and tighten the glute of the kneeling leg. Shift forward slightly until you feel a mild stretch at the front of that hip. Keep ribs stacked over pelvis; avoid arching the lower back.
origin: New addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Place one knee on padding, opposite foot in front.
Gently tuck the tailbone and squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg.
Shift forward a few centimeters while keeping your ribs over your pelvis.

name: Standing split-stance hip flexor stretch
notes: Hold a counter for balance. Step one leg back, bend the front knee slightly, tuck your pelvis, and tighten the rear-leg glute. Keep your trunk upright and shift weight forward slightly.
origin: New addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Hold a counter and step one foot behind you.
Slightly bend the front knee, tuck your pelvis, and squeeze the back glute.
Shift forward gently without arching your back.

name: Gentle supine pelvic tilts
notes: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor. Slowly rock the pelvis to gently flatten then release the lower back. Use a small pain-free range without pushing into symptoms.
origin: New addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet planted.
Exhale and slowly roll your pelvis to reduce the gap under your low back.
Inhale and return to neutral. Repeat in a small comfortable range.

name: Low lunge with arm reach
notes: In a comfortable half-kneeling lunge, gently tuck the pelvis and squeeze the back-leg glute. Raise the arm on the kneeling side overhead only if comfortable, keeping ribs down and avoiding a low-back arch.
origin: New addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Set up a padded half-kneeling lunge.
Tuck your pelvis and engage the back-leg glute.
Reach the arm on the kneeling side overhead without flaring your ribs.

name: Supine single-knee-to-chest, other leg supported
notes: Lie on your back with both knees bent. Draw one knee toward your chest while keeping the other foot on the floor. Breathe and relax; do not force the stretch or straighten the other leg if it increases back symptoms.
origin: New addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Lie on your back with both knees bent.
Bring one knee toward your chest, using hands behind the thigh.
Keep the other foot supported; release slowly and switch sides.

name: Brisk walk to easy jog
notes: Begin with brisk walking, then gradually transition to a comfortable jog. Increase effort gradually; avoid sprinting from a cold start.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Walk briskly with relaxed shoulders.
Increase cadence gradually.
Jog easily only if symptoms remain comfortable.

name: Marching with arm swing
notes: March tall, swinging opposite arms and lifting knees only to a comfortable height.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Stand upright and engage your trunk gently.
Alternate lifting knees while swinging opposite arms.
Keep steps rhythmic without leaning backward.

name: Front-to-back leg swings
notes: Hold a wall or rail. Swing one leg forward and backward in a controlled, small-to-moderate range.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Hold a stable support.
Swing one leg gently forward and back.
Avoid arching the lower back; change sides.

name: Side-to-side leg swings
notes: Hold support and swing one leg gently across the body and out to the side without twisting the trunk.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Face a sturdy support.
Swing one leg across and outward slowly.
Keep hips level and repeat on the other leg.

name: Walking knee hugs
notes: Step forward, briefly lift a knee toward your chest, then release and continue walking. Skip if it provokes sciatic symptoms.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Step forward and stand tall.
Bring one knee up gently, without rounding your back.
Release and switch sides as you walk.

name: Walking heel-to-glute pulls
notes: Walk forward, briefly bending a knee to bring heel toward buttock. Avoid forcing the knee or arching the back.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Take a slow step.
Bend the trailing knee and briefly hold the ankle only if comfortable.
Release and alternate sides.

name: Lateral side steps
notes: Keep knees softly bent and take controlled side steps to activate hips and glutes.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Step sideways, keeping knees aligned with toes.
Repeat in the other direction.

name: Walking lunges, short stride
notes: Use a short, controlled stride and shallow depth. Hold a rail if needed; skip if knee or back pain increases.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Step forward into a short split stance.
Bend knees slightly while keeping torso upright.
Push through the front foot and alternate.

name: Calf raises and ankle bounces
notes: Raise heels smoothly to warm calves and ankles; keep it low impact.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Stand near a wall for balance.
Rise onto toes and lower slowly.
Keep motion gentle, avoiding painful bouncing.

name: Easy running strides
notes: Only when symptom-free and preparing for a faster run: accelerate smoothly to a moderate pace, not an all-out sprint.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Start at an easy jog.
Gradually increase pace to controlled moderate speed.
Walk to recover; omit if pain or tingling develops.

name: Supine hamstring stretch with strap
notes: Lie on your back and raise one leg using a strap behind the thigh or foot. Keep knee slightly bent; avoid pulling into nerve tingling.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Lie on your back with one knee bent and foot supported.
Raise the other leg comfortably using a strap.
Hold a mild stretch behind thigh, then switch sides.

name: Standing hamstring hinge
notes: With soft knees, hinge at the hips and return upright. Keep spine neutral; do not chase a deep stretch.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Push hips backward while keeping back neutral.
Stand tall by engaging glutes.

name: Supine active knee extension
notes: Lie on back, hold thigh behind knee with hip comfortably bent, slowly straighten and bend knee without provoking nerve symptoms.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Lie on your back with both knees bent.
Hold one thigh behind knee and slowly extend lower leg.
Return to bent knee and repeat, switching sides.

name: Gentle sciatic nerve slider
notes: Optional only if recommended by a clinician. Slowly extend knee while pointing toes, then bend knee while bringing toes toward shin. Never hold a nerve stretch or push into symptoms.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Lie comfortably on your back with one thigh supported.
Gently extend knee while pointing toes away.
Bend knee while flexing ankle; stop if symptoms worsen.

name: Hamstring bridge heel dig
notes: Lie on your back with knees bent and heels planted. Gently dig heels into floor and lift hips a little to engage posterior chain.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Lie on your back with heels on floor.
Press heels down and lift hips a comfortable amount.
Lower slowly without arching your back.

name: Hamstring isometric heel press
notes: With knee bent and heel planted, gently press heel into floor without moving the leg. This strengthens hamstrings without aggressive stretching.
origin: New evidence-informed general exercise addition, not from scanned handouts
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Press one heel into floor at a comfortable effort.
Hold briefly, relax, and change sides.
